title: Rider Violet — work-log and composer correction
question: This revision removes persistent speaker identity and restores clear composer hierarchy. Review the three states together, then choose a screen and note whether the suite is approved or needs another adjustment.

options.label: Work-log Workbench
options.lineage: Rider visual clarity + T3 message behavior + cw-code tooling
options.thesis: User prompts identify themselves through right alignment; agent output remains open on the canvas. No names, avatars, or timestamps interrupt the work log.
options.viewport: The composer regains a substantial writing plane and a clearly visible second-tone tooling shelf without separators or segmented boxes.
options.risk: Hover and keyboard-focus affordances must make message timestamp/copy actions discoverable without reintroducing persistent chrome.

options.label: Settings Window
options.lineage: Rider settings clarity + focused overlay workflow
options.thesis: Configuration opens as a substantial focused window over an inert workbench, without making the project sidebar part of the settings layout.
options.viewport: The overlay contains only settings categories, provider roster, and provider detail. The workbench survives as subdued context around the edges.
options.risk: The large overlay must trap focus cleanly and keep background session activity visible but non-interactive.

options.label: Agents Work-log
options.lineage: Rider workbench + T3 message behavior + full-width agent trace
options.thesis: The same label-free work log and restored composer carry into the multi-agent state, with the compact roster above a full-width inspector.
options.viewport: The center conversation stays readable while the right pane preserves the improved vertical agent overview and selected-agent trace.
options.risk: The overview must remain capped and independently scrollable when many agents are active.
